On July 24, 2026, Lien Finance (an Ethereum DeFi structured products protocol) was exploited. The attacker abused a validation flaw in the exchangeEquivalentBonds function of the BondMakerCollateralizedEth contract (missing multiset integrity checks), minting unbacked bond tokens and draining approximately $542K USDC via OTC pools.

On 23 July 2026, Lien Finance on Ethereum Mainnet was exploited via a permissionless bond group registration flaw and inadequate input validation that enabled an attacker to mint unbacked bond tokens, manipulate OTC pool pricing, and extract approximately $542,144 in USDC from protocol liquidity pools. The Lien protocol failed to adequately validate bond group registration and exchange logic in its GeneralizedDotc OTC pools. The bond group registration was permissionless, and the rate calculation function did not check for the economic legitimacy of new bond groups, enabling arbitrary creation and redemption of unbacked bond tokens.
